FALLS TOWNSHIP


RESOLUTION NO. 2026-11


A RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF SUPERVISORS OF FALLS TOWNSHIP, BUCKS COUNTY, PENNSYLVANIA DECLARING A PORTION OF THE FALLS TOWNSHIP ZONING ORDINANCE SUBSTANTIVELY INVALID AND PROPOSING TO PREPARE A CURATIVE AMENDMENT TO CURE SUCH INVALIDITY PURSUANT TO SECTION 609.2 OF THE MUNICIPALITIES PLANNING CODE

Commonly referred to as a “curative amendment,” township attorney Lauren Gallagher called it a “protective measure for any substantive validity challenge” that would potentially be filed within the 180-day period that the township has designated for review and possible changes to its zoning ordinance.

RESOLUTION #9-26: Mr. Brenneman advised of the proposed Resolution declaring the 2019

Amended and Restated Little Britain Township Zoning Ordinance substantively invalid insofar as it

excludes data centers and ancillary buildings or uses, including but not limited to energy generating

facilities. The proposed Resolution is to allow the township to begin a curative amendment process as

authorized by section 609.2 of the Municipal Planning Code. Following a review of this information,

the meeting was open for public comment, with no response. A motion was then made by Mr. Beiler,

seconded by Mr. Coates and carried to adopt Resolution #9-26.

4.10 Jenny Picciano – – Vote to approve Resolution 2026-16.

Mr. Mussina moved to approve. Mr. Sortman 2nd the motion. Approved 3-0
